situation: `--all` against a board of 40 open cards, one of which sits in no column. Rendering every row at the 100-word bound would total far more than the standing check's ceiling.
expected_guard: all 40 cards appear as rows, in board order; no description exceeds 100 words; there is no total ceiling; the uncolumned card is a row marked as such rather than an omission
must_not: drop a card to fit any budget — the bound is per row and there is no total
report SNAPSHOT-CLIPPED, which in this mode means something was dropped
apply the standing check's 200-word total to this mode
omit the uncolumned card, which belongs to no section and does belong in this table
why_this_fixture_exists: The two modes bound themselves differently and the difference is the whole reason both exist. A total ceiling here would silently drop cards from a read whose entire purpose is saying what is there.
